title: _molt_realpath falls back to python3: resolve in shell (Molt ships no Python)
body:
`lib/molt.sh:155`: when `realpath(1)` is not on PATH, `_molt_realpath` runs `python3 -c 'import os,sys; print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))'`. hv, 23 Oct 2026: ship no Python in any repo; zsh, bespoke Rust, or Elixir or an escript where the task warrants it, which Molt's never does (the user-scope AGENTS.md since Molt-matts e5c9e68).

Resolve in shell, on every platform, so one code path runs everywhere and the tests cover the one that ships: follow the symlink chain with plain `readlink` (no `-f`, which BSD lacks), relative targets joined to the link's directory, and name the result's directory with `molt_disk_path`, the resolver the home guard already agrees with. The contract stays: `$1` back unchanged when it cannot be resolved. `molt_same_file` is the only caller.

Also seen, not in scope: `molt_link` (`lib/molt.sh:279`) compares two `readlink -f` outputs, which are both empty where `readlink -f` is missing, so any symlink would read as already linked there; `molt_link_points_to` is the comparison it wants. `liberators/editors.sh:9` uses `readlink -f` too, on sleeves that have it.
